description: A simple shelf protector that shields a fragile or metal-fitted binding and its neighbours from abrasion. Lined millboard is placed beside the book, or a piece is bent round it and reinforced at the folds with linen, then slipped onto the shelf with the open end outward so it is barely visible. For valuable volumes a lettered case may be built to carry the title on its back.
name: protective case

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive
